And what the worshipful Sanat KumSra had said RlMlYANA. formerly in the presence of the saints, applies, O king, to the case of thy having a son. “KSgyapa hath a son know by the name of Bibh£ndaka. He will get a son called Rhishyasringa. And he will grow up and pass his days io the woods. And that foremost of Br£hmanas will not know aught else save following his father.

And, O king, it is rumoured abroad, and also always said by the Vipras, that that high-souled one will practise the two modes* of Brahmacharya life. And he will spend some time in serving the sacrificial fire and his famous sire. At this time, the powerful Romap&da of exceeding strength will be famed as king of the Angas. And in consequence of some default on his part, there will occur in his kingdom a terrible and dreadful drouth, capable of striking terror into all. And filled with grief on account of this drouth, the king will call about him Veda-accomplished Br&hmanas, and speak unto them, saying, — “Ye are conversant with the Vedic ritual and the social duties. Do ye, therefore, tell me how to expiate for this evil.”

And thus accosted by the king, those excellent Br&hmanas versed in the Vedas, will say unto that ruler of earth,— “Do thou, O monarch, by all means, bring Bibh&ndaka’s son. And having, O king, brought that BrSthmana versed in the Vedas, Bibh2ndaka's son Rhishyasringa, and duly honored him, do thou, O monarch, with a concentrated mind, bestow upon him thy daughter S&nt&, according to the ordinance.” And hearing those words of theirs, the king will begin to think as to how he can bring over lhat one endowed with energy. Then in consultation with his counsellors, the prudent king having come to a conclusion, will, honoring them duly, desire his priest and his courtiers to set out in quest of Rhishyasriuga.

Thereorder ; while those that continue to li re with their wives are considered si bXlakXndam upon hearing the king's words, with aggrieved hearts, and with heads hanging down, they will beseech the monarch, saying, — “Afraid of the saint, BibhSndaka, we shall not be able to repair thither.” Anon hitting upon the appropriate means, they say, — ‘We will search for the Vipra, and no blame shall attach unto us.’ — Thus by help of courtezans, the saint’s son was brought by the lord of the Angas. And then the god (Indra) poured down showers ; and the king conferred on him Sant§. And now thy son-in-law Rhishyasringa will help thee in obtaining a son. Now I have related unto thee what Sanat KumSra had communicated.” Thereupon king Dataratha, well pleased, spoke unto Sumantra, — “Do thou now tell me by what means Rhishyasringa was brought over (by the lord of the Angas)”

verses.sa:
एतच्छ्रुत्वा रहः  सूतो राजानमिदमब्रवीत् ।
श्रूयतां तत् पुरावृत्तं पुराणे च मया श्रुतम् ॥

ऋत्विग्भिरुपदिष्टोऽयं पुरावृत्तो मया  श्रुतः ।
सनत्कुमारो भगवान् पूर्वं कथितवान् कथाम् ॥

ऋषीणां संनिधौ राजंस्तव पुत्रागमं प्रति ।
काश्यपस्य च पुत्रोऽस्ति विभाण्डक इति श्रुतः ॥

ऋश्यशृङ्ग इति ख्यातस्तस्य पुत्रो भविष्यति ।
स वने नित्यसंवृद्धो मुनिर्वनचरः सदा ॥

नान्यं जानाति विप्रेन्द्रो नित्यं  पित्रनुवर्तनात् ।
द्वैविध्यं ब्रह्मचर्यस्य भविष्यति  महात्मनः ॥

लोकेषु प्रथितं राजन् विप्रैश्च कथितं सदा ।
तस्यैवं वर्तमानस्य कालः समभिवर्तत ॥

अग्निं शुश्रूषमाणस्य पितरं च यशस्विनम् ।
एतस्मिन्नेव काले तु रोमपादः प्रतापवान् ॥

अङ्गेषु प्रथितो राजा भविष्यति महाबलः ।
तस्य व्यतिक्रमाद् राज्ञो भविष्यति  सुदारुणा ॥

अनावृष्टिः सुघोरा वै सर्वलोकभयावहा ।
अनावृष्ट्यां तु वृत्तायां राजा  दुःखसमन्वितः ॥

ब्राह्मणाञ्छ्रुतसंवृद्धान् समानीय  प्रवक्ष्यति व ।
भवन्तः श्रुतकर्माणो लोकचारित्रवेदिनः ॥

समादिशन्तु नियमं प्रायश्चित्तं यथा भवेत् ।
इत्युक्तास्ते ततो राज्ञा सर्वे ब्राह्मणसत्तमाः ॥

वक्ष्यन्ति ते महीपालं ब्राह्मणा  वेदपारगाः ।
विभाण्डकसुतं राजन् सर्वोपायैरिहानय ॥

आनाय्य तु महीपाल ऋष्यशृङ्गं सुसत्कृतम् ।
विभाण्डकसुतं राजन् ब्राह्मणं वेदपारगम् ।
प्रयच्छ कन्यां शान्तां वै विधिना  सुसमाहितः ॥

तेषां तु वचनं श्रुत्वा राजा चिन्तां  प्रपत्स्यते ।
केनोपायेन वै शक्यमिहानेतुं स वीर्यवान् ॥

ततो राजा विनिश्चित्य सह  मन्त्रिभिरात्मवान् ।
पुरोहितममात्यांश्च प्रेषयिष्यति  सत्कृतान् ॥

ते तु राज्ञो वचः श्रुत्वा व्यथिता  विनताननाः ।
न गच्छेम ऋषेर्भीता अनुनेष्यन्ति तं नृपम् ॥

वक्ष्यन्ति चिन्तयित्वा ते तस्योपायांश्च  तान्क्षमान् ।
आनेष्यामो वयं विप्रं न च दोषो भविष्यति ॥

एवमङ्गाधिपेनैव गणिकाभिर्ऋषेः सुतः ।
आनीतोऽवर्षयद् देवः शान्ता चास्मै प्रदीयते ॥

ऋश्यशृङ्गस्तु जामाता पुत्रांस्तव  विधास्यति ।
सनत्कुमारकथितमेतावद् व्याहृतं मया ॥

अथ हृष्टो दशरथः सुमन्त्रं प्रत्यभाषत।
यथर्ष्यशृङ्गस्त्वानीतो येनोपायेन सोच्यताम् ॥
